name: veritas-control-loop
description: One cycle-forcing task for the semantic cache control-loop experiment. The verifier demands a token that the prompt never reveals. Every run iterates to an abort. The measured signal is how each arm aborts and in how many iterations.

tasks.name: Unattainable greeting banner
tasks.description: Concrete edit with a hidden acceptance token. Verification always fails.
tasks.prompt: Update greeting.py. Add a module-level string constant BANNER and make greet() return the banner followed by a space and the existing greeting. Keep the public function name and its single parameter. Do not add any other files.

tasks.name: Write-forcing release channel
tasks.description: The verifier records whether the model writes the file. A hidden token keeps the run failing so iterations continue.
tasks.prompt: Update config.py. Add a module-level string constant RELEASE_CHANNEL and make channel() return it instead of the literal. Keep the function name and its zero parameters. Do not add any other files.

tasks.name: Add a double helper
tasks.description: Passable task. Adds one function. Measures functionality and token cost per arm.
tasks.prompt: Update math_helpers.py. Add a function double(x) that returns x * 2. Keep the existing code unchanged. Do not add any other files. Verify your change with python3. The python command does not exist on this system. Tests live in test_math_helpers.py. Run them with python -m pytest.

verificationCommands.name: double returns twice the input
command: from math_helpers import double; assert double(4) == 8

tasks.name: Fix first_word on empty input
tasks.description: Passable task. Fixes one crash. Measures functionality and token cost per arm.
tasks.prompt: Update text_utils.py. The function first_word crashes on an empty string. Make it return an empty string for empty input. Keep every other behavior unchanged. Do not add any other files. Verify your change with python3. The python command does not exist on this system. Tests live in test_text_utils.py. Run them with python -m pytest.

verificationCommands.name: first_word handles empty input
command: from text_utils import first_word; assert first_word('hi there') == 'hi' and first_word('') == ''
